subject.title: feature: system event priority/bypass-queue mode for reliable in-session alerts

question: Should urgent `system event` delivery become an immediate operator-visible alert, a prompt-visible transcript injection path, or two separate paths with distinct ordering and trust contracts?
rationale: Current code intentionally defers prompt-visible system-event delivery while the session lane is active, and bypassing that guard would change both product semantics and prompt-injection/session-ordering boundaries.

options.title: Split alert and transcript paths
options.body: Add an immediate operator-visible alert path for TUI/control surfaces while keeping prompt-visible system events ordered through a reviewed queue or drain contract.

options.title: Allow prompt-visible priority injection
options.body: Add an explicit high-priority prompt/transcript event mode with strict authorization, ordering semantics, and regression tests for active turns.

options.title: Defer to scheduler fairness
options.body: Keep `system event` best-effort for now and solve foreground/background ordering through the broader session-lane policy tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/54488.

recommendation.title: Split alert and transcript paths
recommendation.body: Add an immediate operator-visible alert path for TUI/control surfaces while keeping prompt-visible system events ordered through a reviewed queue or drain contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-history owner for the CLI, wake RPC, heartbeat, and system-event trust boundary touched by this decision.
